properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — the boundary question underneath dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph, 2026-08-11. Separate node because it has an answer whichever way that one goes. Nothing here is intent.

THE OBSERVATION: reflow2's outward-facing docs are not one kind of thing, and rendering the wrong ones would hollow them out.

  PROJECTABLE — the content IS graph state, and every staleness found today lives here
    three-axes.md      what the schema holds on each axis; the status column is a COUNT
    overview.md        the type counts, the reading order, what is built vs planned
    genesis.md         what the genesis tool does and what it returns
    artifact-linking.md    what link_artifact / reconcile_artifacts return
    impact-propagation.md  what propagate_from returns — a worked blast radius IS an example
    gap-surfacing.md   what detect_gaps returns, and the live gap list
    heal-process.md    what propose_heal returns
    viewpoints.md      the catalogue itself is a table of what renders

  IRREDUCIBLE ARGUMENT — no graph query produces this, and a rendered version would be worse
    vision.md          the four lifecycle transitions and WHY they break. An argument, not data.
    partnership.md     the LLM failure-mode taxonomy. Most of it is not in the graph and should
                       not be — "sycophancy" is not a node type. Its value is the reasoning.
    operating-environment.md   the Kennewick-vs-Mars argument for why environments matter, about
                       a layer with ZERO instances — so a projection would render an empty page
                       for the doc that explains why the layer should exist at all.

⭐ THE THIRD CASE IS THE INTERESTING ONE AND IT BREAKS THE SIMPLE SPLIT. `operating-environment.md` argues for a capability that has never been used. A pure projection of it renders nothing, because there is nothing to project — the doc's whole job is to explain something the graph does NOT yet hold. Any rendering scheme has to allow a doc to be ABOUT AN ABSENCE without confessing itself into uselessness. The same is true of every doc describing planned work.

⭐ AND THE SPLIT IS NOT PER-DOC, IT IS PER-PARAGRAPH. `overview.md` is mostly reading order and argument, with one sentence carrying "29 node types, 60 edge types" — which is the sentence that went wrong. `three-axes.md` is mostly explanation with one STATUS COLUMN that is wrong. So the natural unit is a SECTION, not a file, which is the argument for option (c) in the parent node — embed rendered blocks in prose — rather than rendering whole documents.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Per-section markers: prose files with fenced regions regenerated from a named tool call, and a CI check that re-renders and diffs. Facts under the gate, argument left alone, absence expressible because the prose around the block says what the empty block means.
(b) Two doc classes with different rules — `docs/rendered/` regenerated wholesale and gate-checked, `docs/` hand-written and exempt. Cleaner to enforce, and it splits a reader's attention across two directories.
(c) Render everything and accept that argument-shaped docs become thin. Rejected on sight here, recorded so nobody re-proposes it: it would delete the reasoning that is the most valuable content reflow2 has.
(d) Render nothing; instead add a CHECK that every factual claim in a doc matches the graph. Keeps all prose, needs the claims to be machine-identifiable — which is `check_doc_versions.py` generalised beyond version strings, and that tool already proves the pattern works (it FAILS when a pattern matches nothing, so rewording a doc breaks the build loudly instead of silently disabling the check).

📌 (d) IS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS AND IS NOT MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE WITH (a). `tools/check_doc_versions.py` is already a CI gate that asserts doc claims against the build, anchored on literal phrases, deliberately failing when a pattern matches nothing. Extending its anchors from version strings to type counts would have caught `overview.md`'s "60 edge types" this morning for the cost of one line.
properties.name: OPEN — which outward-facing docs can NEVER be a projection, and how do rendered facts and irreducible argument sit together on one page?
properties.rationale: Rendering the docs is not one decision — some docs ARE graph state, some are argument no query produces, and one (operating-environment) argues for a layer with zero instances, so a projection of it renders an empty page. The natural unit turns out to be a section rather than a file, which changes what the parent question is actually choosing between.
